why: A build lane reported three families BLOCKED_SOURCE on bytes that are held. The cause was not custody and not the packets: it was the shape of the worktrees I provisioned. This records the fact so no lane loses another shift to it.
theFact: private/ is a mounted source custody holding 868 MB of official-form bytes, and it is NOT a git path. .gitignore line 53 ignores private/, so it exists only where it was materialised. `git sparse-checkout add private` can never produce it, and its absence from a checkout proves nothing about whether the bytes are held.
theResolverConsequence: scripts/lib/corpus-index-paths.mjs resolves any custody declared pathsRelativeTo: "repositoryRoot" inside the running checkout. From a worktree without private/, it reports genuinely held sources as unmounted. That is a resolver artefact rather than a custody fact, and it hits every family whose sources sit under human_source_returns or d_source_packs -- not only the lane that found it.
whatIDid: Symlinked private/ into every lane worktree that lacked it: pfa, pfc, pfd, pfe, pf14, pf23, src1. Zero disk cost, and the path is gitignored so no lane can commit it by accident. The shared lane brief now says this in the sparse-checkout section.
whyNotACodeChange: Adding a second resolution mechanism -- an env-root fallback per custody -- would leave two ways to answer the same question and a lane could satisfy one while failing the other. The custody is supposed to be mounted at the checkout root; mounting it there is the fix. A code change would be warranted only if a custody genuinely cannot be mounted.
whatThisDoesNotSay: Nothing here says any particular source is held. It says a lane that reports one unmounted from a worktree without private/ has measured its own checkout, not custody. Every source binding is still by content digest.
foundBy: PF24, from three families it stopped and then re-checked against the real mount
